title: Workload stress orchestra and CI canary anchors for kernel/attention perf
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a stress-oriented benchmarking harness (the 'orchestra') and a small set of CI canary anchors that exercise kernel-selection heuristics, attention kernel variants, and prefill/decode scheduling. Deliverables: 1) a reproducible workload stress orchestrator that composes micro-templates (short, mid, long sequences; heavy KV reuse; multi-turn chat; reranking) into deterministically seeded runs, 2) a compact set of golden anchor runs for CI (fast, medium, slow) with acceptance thresholds that detect regressions in 95th/99th latency and per-token cost, and 3) integration into CI with auto-skip rules and telemetry hooks to capture kernel routing distributions and attention kernel hit-rate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestra can run 1000 deterministic seeds across three hardware targets (A100-80GB, H100, T4) and produce an artifact with per-run: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel-selection breakdown, attention-kernel-hit-rate, and KV cache hit-rate; 2) CI anchors run in <= 12 minutes on CI runners and fail build when p95 latency regresses >6% or per-token cost regresses >5% compared to golden baseline; 3) Alerts created in PagerDuty when CI anchor fails three consecutive runs; 4) Dashboard tile created in Console showing kernel-selection trend and attention-variant adoption over last 30 days.
test_plan:
- Construct micro-templates: chat-short (<=64), chat-medium (128-512), long-prefill (>=1024), multi-turn-with-kv (simulated 8-turn convo), rerank-batch (10 candidates).
- Compose stress mixes: 70/20/10 short/medium/long; heavy-KV mix: 40/40/20; decode-heavy: 10% long-prefill + 90% decode bursts.
- Golden baselines: capture three seeds per mix on stable runtime-1.19 with quantization profiles Q4 and Q8 and save kernel routing map.
- CI anchor selection: pick one fast mix (short-heavy), one balanced mix (mixed), one slow mix (long-prefill-heavy). Run anchors on an isolated CI GPU pool seeded with golden baseline.
- Metrics collected: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tail-quantiles over sliding window, tokens/sec, per-token GPU time, kernel routing fingerprint (histogram of kernel IDs), attention-kernel hit-rate (optimized vs fallback), KV cache hit-rate, and decode scheduling backlog.
- Run cadence: orchestra weekly for full sweep; CI anchors on every merge to main and nightly stability runs.
- Synthetic noise: inject 1-2% stochastic delay to emulate host jitter; include deterministic seed to ensure reproducibility.
design_decisions:
- Deterministic seeding chosen over pure stochastic runs to allow CI-level baselines and regression diffs.
- Use a compact kernel fingerprint (sorted top-10 kernel IDs + weights) rather than full trace to keep artifacts small.
- Trade-off: shorter CI anchors to minimize CI time will focus on p95 sensitivity; full weekly orchestra handles p99.
- Attention metrics instrumented at kernel boundary to avoid high-cardinality traces in production telemetry.
- Orchestator runs will not attempt full runtime scheduling changes; it will record the runtime's observed scheduling and re-run after candidate scheduler changes for comparison.
implementation_notes:
- Add new harness module: rl_bench/orchestra (Python) that emits JSONL artifacts per seed and an aggregated summary csv.
- Extend existing CI job template (ci/runtime-perf-anchor.yml) to run three anchors with resource tagging and to push artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/golden/ENG-99501/.
- Runtime telemetry: add a short-lived flag to collect kernel-selection summaries per-request and expose via promo telemetry api for harness consumption.
- Provide a migration shim that maps old kernel IDs (pre-1.18 renumbering) to new IDs for historical comparison.
- Implement comparator script tools/compare_baselines.py that computes relative regressions and generates human-readable and machine-readable outputs for CI.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: CI flakiness due to noisy hardware. Mitigation: require 3 consecutive failures to open incident; use median of three quick repeats in CI anchor.
- Risk: high cardinality of kernel traces. Mitigation: fingerprint to top-k and compress artifact.
- Risk: false positives when quantization profiles change. Mitigation: baseline includes quantization profile metadata; comparator will only compare runs with matching profile unless explicitly overridden.
- Risk: unintentional rollout blocking. Mitigation: add auto-skip tag for releases flagged urgent and route to manual review rather than auto-fail.
rollout_plan:
- Week 1: deliver harness and three CI anchors behind feature flag; smoke runs on canary CI pool.
- Week 2: onboard kernel-selection telemetry and storage; capture first golden baselines on runtime-1.19.
- Week 3: flip CI anchors on for main branch; monitor false-positive rate for 7 days.
- Week 4: publish dashboard tiles and create runbook for on-call.
- Post-rollout: iterate thresholds based on observed distribution; add more anchors for diverse hardware if needed.
